fatal_errors: The proposed material is a single-phase solid solution, whereas the target is an as-cast dual-phase AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic alloy containing FCC and B2 phases.
The intervention is an undefined placeholder rather than a specified thermal-aging treatment near 600°C or 750°C.
No temperature window, exposure duration, or loading regime is defined.
The proposed grain-size and grain-boundary-cohesion mechanism does not capture L12 ordering, increased APBE, planar slip, jagged B2/FCC phase boundaries, or phase-boundary crack initiation.
The prediction of generic toughness improvement misses the non-monotonic ductile-brittle-ductile transition, including minimum ductility after aging near 600°C and recovery near 750°C.
No prior observations or cited evidence support the hypothesis.
The stated falsification test, 'Experiment Y,' has no procedure, measurement, control, or rejection criterion.
explanation: The response only restates the broad goal of preserving toughness after thermal exposure and loading. Its intervention, conditions, mechanism, boundary, evidence, and falsification experiment are placeholders rather than a testable materials hypothesis. Although comparison with the same untreated alloy is a minimally appropriate control, the response neither reconstructs the target thermal-aging phenomenon nor offers a sufficiently specified plausible alternative.
